label: conj:os-reflection-positivity-from-reeb
title: Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb $\mathbb{Z}_2$
html:
The Yang–Mills surreal bound gives the mass-gap statement at substrate order \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3 but explicitly defers the Wightman-axiom portion of the Millennium Prize statement—the regularity programme of recovering a standard renormalised QFT as the standard part of the q-deformed substrate. This conjecture supplies the bridge: the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2 acting on the Frobenius pairing furnishes Osterwalder–Schrader reflection positivity in the archimedean realisation. Together with the surreal mass gap, this forms the Osterwalder–Schrader sufficient input for Wightman reconstruction.

Conjecture (OS reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2). Let \theta denote the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 \subset U(1)_{\xi} inside the Reeb U(1)—equivalently, the chart-swap involution \iota : Z \mapsto Z^{-1} on the contact affine chart at \varTheta = \pi, per chart-swap U(1) is the Reeb flow. Then the Frobenius pairing \langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle_F on A satisfies reflection positivity under \theta:

\langle \theta(\phi), \phi \rangle_F \geq 0 \qquad \text{for every state } \phi \in A_+,

with equality if and only if \phi vanishes on the positive-time half of the Reeb decomposition. Under the archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, this categorical positivity descends to the Osterwalder–Schrader reflection-positivity axiom of the four Euclidean Wightman correlation functions \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\langle \phi_1 \cdots \phi_n \rangle_F\bigr) on the \varepsilon \to 0 standard manifold \mathbb{R}^4.

The Osterwalder–Schrader reflection \theta_{\mathrm{OS}} on Euclidean spacetime is reflection in the \tau = 0 hyperplane, i.e., (x_1, x_2, x_3, \tau) \mapsto (x_1, x_2, x_3, -\tau). In the categorical contact-geometric formulation, Euclidean time is the Reeb parameter t along \xi (categorical Reeb derivation), so \theta_{\mathrm{OS}} acts on the contact affine chart as \phi_t \mapsto \phi_{-t}. The categorical realisation of this involution is precisely the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 subgroup at \varTheta = \pi of the chart-swap U(1) family \rho_\varTheta : z \mapsto e^{i\varTheta} z. The chart-swap–Reeb identification shows this coincides with the Reeb flow U(1). We require no separate OS reflection to construct: it is already present in the categorical infrastructure as the \mathbb{Z}_2 subgroup of the Reeb circle.

The Frobenius pairing is symmetric by construction: \Psi = S^2 = \mathrm{id}_A, so \langle a, b \rangle_F = \langle b, a \rangle_F. Under the \theta-action on A, the antipode S swaps the two factors and inverts the Reeb flow direction. Symmetry of the Frobenius pairing under \Psi implies \theta-invariance of the pairing up to the sign captured by the Reeb-half decomposition. The conjecture is the positivity statement: for any state \phi supported on the positive-time Reeb half, \langle \theta(\phi), \phi \rangle_F evaluates to a non-negative scalar in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}). This positivity refines the symmetry. Symmetry alone gives \langle \theta(\phi), \phi \rangle_F = \langle \phi, \theta(\phi) \rangle_F (so the quantity is real), but does not force the real value to be non-negative. We require the structural input that the antipode-twisted pairing \langle \theta(\cdot), \cdot \rangle_F descends through \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} to a positive-definite inner product on the half-line L^2(\mathbb{R}_{>0}).

The Osterwalder–Schrader theorem states that a family of Euclidean correlation functions \{S_n\} on \mathbb{R}^4 defines a Wightman QFT on Minkowski space if and only if (OS0) temperedness, (OS1) Euclidean covariance, (OS2) reflection positivity, (OS3) symmetry, and (OS4) cluster decomposition all hold.

In the QOU framework:

OS axiom QOU input
OS0 (temperedness) \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} images of partial products \Phi_n are tempered by the archimedean limit conjecture at every x \in (0, 1).
OS1 (Euclidean covariance) S_5-action on Bring's coordinate ring is the categorical lift of the \mathrm{SO}(4) / \mathrm{Spin}(4) rotation group, and the \mathbb{Z}_2 \hookrightarrow U(1)_{\xi} hierarchy is the Euclidean time translation.
OS2 (reflection positivity) This conjecture.
OS3 (symmetry / locality) Categorical permutation symmetry of the Frobenius pairing; \Psi = S^2 = \mathrm{id}_A.
OS4 (cluster decomposition) Mass gap \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3 from the surreal bound gives exponential clustering at separation r: \vert S_n(\cdots) - S_k(\cdots) S_{n-k}(\cdots)\vert \lesssim e^{-\Delta_q r}.

OS0, OS1, OS3 are categorically built-in. OS4 is the surreal mass-gap statement. OS2 is the open input—this conjecture. Granting it, the OS theorem reconstructs a Wightman QFT on \mathbb{R}^4 as the standard part of the q-deformed substrate, completing the Wightman-axiom portion of the Yang–Mills millennium statement.

The positivity statement involves three open ingredients:

  1. Categorical positivity of the antipode-twisted pairing. The Frobenius pairing is constructively non-degenerate, but neither the QOU axioms nor the Frobenius–Hopf substrate definition currently impose positivity of \langle \theta(\cdot), \cdot \rangle_F. The conjecture claims the substrate, being a C^*-Frobenius–Hopf algebra in the archimedean specialisation (q = q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1}), inherits positivity from the C^*-norm.
  2. Stability under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}. The archimedean realisation functor must commute with the positivity restriction: \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\langle\theta(\phi),\phi\rangle_F\bigr) = \bigl\langle\theta_{\mathrm{OS}}\tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\phi),\, \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\phi)\bigr\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^4)}. Equivalently, the OS reflection on the standard Euclidean correlation functions is the \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}-image of the Reeb antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 action. This follows from the chart-swap–Reeb identification once \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} preserves the U(1)_{\xi}-action on contact charts.
  3. Mathlib infrastructure. A complete proof requires a Frobenius structure on the categorical C^*-completion and the Wightman reconstruction theorem—neither in Mathlib today. The conjecture is packaged as the typeclass QOU.AppendixSurreals.OSReflectionPositivity, with one field stating the positivity inequality. Granting the class instance, the surreal bound completes OS reconstruction.

Ingredients (2) and (3) are technical plumbing once the categorical content is settled. The only genuinely new mathematical input needed is a single positivity axiom on the substrate Frobenius algebra. A Frobenius algebra (A, \mu, \eta, \Delta, \varepsilon) in a C^*-tensor category is positive if its evaluation map \eta : \mathbf{1} \to A admits a state-positive lift—i.e., the composition

\mathbf{1} \xrightarrow{\;\eta\;} A \xrightarrow{\;\Delta\;} A \otimes A \xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{id}\,\otimes\,*\;} A \otimes A^*

factors through the positive cone of A \otimes A^*. The missing input is exactly this:

Axiom (substrate C^*-Frobenius positivity). At the archimedean substrate value q = q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1}, the Frobenius–Hopf substrate A admits a C^*-completion in which the unit map \eta : \mathbf{1} \to A is positive in the categorical sense above. Equivalently, (A, \mu, \eta, \Delta, \varepsilon) is a positive Frobenius algebra in the C^*-tensor category \mathbf{C} at q_0.

Granting the substrate C^*-Frobenius positivity axiom, along with prop:reeb-u1-chart-swap and def:archimedean-realization-functor, OS axiom (OS2) holds: \langle\theta(\phi), \phi\rangle_F \geq 0 for every state \phi in the positive-time Reeb half.

The proof sketch involves three steps:

  1. Categorical reflection = Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2. By prop:reeb-u1-chart-swap, \theta is the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 \subset T_q subgroup acting on the contact-affine chart \mathbb{P}(V) via z \mapsto -z. On the substrate Hopf algebra A, the action \theta_A : A \to A factors through the antipode S via the T_q-grading: \theta_A = S \circ (\mathrm{sign}\,\text{of}\,\xi\text{-grading}).
  2. Antipode-twisted pairing = state-positive form. The substrate Frobenius pairing factors through the antipode by \langle a, b \rangle_F = \varepsilon(\mu(a, S(b))). Composing with \theta_A: \langle \theta(\phi), \phi \rangle_F = \varepsilon(\mu(\theta(\phi), S(\phi))) = \varepsilon(\mu(S(\phi^*), S(\phi))) where \phi^* is the C^*-conjugate. By the substrate positivity axiom, this evaluates to a non-negative element of \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}) = k.
  3. Stability under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}. \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} sends the categorical C^*-norm to the standard L^2-norm on \mathbb{R}^4 by construction. Positivity is preserved.

The status of OS reflection positivity in the QOU framework is equal to the status of this single C^*-Frobenius positivity axiom. The axiom is well-formulated inside unitary fusion categories and unitary C^*-Frobenius algebras. Verifying that the QOU substrate A at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1} satisfies it requires:

  • A choice of C^*-norm on A compatible with the q_0-deformation.
  • Verification that one of these candidate norms makes the Frobenius pairing positive in the sense above.
  • Compatibility of the chosen norm with the antipode S.

This follow-up programme is formalised as conj:wenzl-positivity-implies-substrate-positivity. Closing that bridge conjecture makes the substrate axiom derived from Wenzl's classical result, discharging the OS-reflection-positivity-as-axiom assumption.

The Wightman-axiom portion of the Yang–Mills millennium statement reduces to the structural positivity of the antipode-twisted Frobenius pairing. The reflection involved is the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 subgroup of the Reeb U(1), made visible by the chart-swap–Reeb identification. The categorical infrastructure already houses every OS ingredient except this positivity.
